quickSummary: STIs / RTIs: Bacterial (Syphilis - Treponema, Gonorrhea - Neisseria, Chlamydiasis - Chlamydia: all CURABLE with antibiotics), Viral (AIDS - HIV, Hepatitis B - HBV, Genital Herpes - HSV-2: all INCURABLE), Protozoan (Trichomoniasis - Trichomonas: CURABLE with Metronidazole). summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: STIs (Sexually Transmitted Infections / RTIs) are transmitted through sexual contact. Bacterial STIs (Syphilis, Gonorrhea, Chlamydia) and Protozoan STIs (Trichomoniasis) are CURABLE with antibiotics/antiprotozoals. Viral STIs (HIV/AIDS, Hepatitis B, Genital Herpes, HPV) are INCURABLE. Untreated STIs lead to Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID), ectopic gestation, stillbirths, cervical carcinoma, and permanent infertility.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 8.1 Comprehensive STI Pathogen & Clinical Matrix

| Disease Name | Etiological Pathogen | Pathogen Category | Clinical Manifestations | Curability Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Syphilis** | *Treponema pallidum* | Spirochete Bacteria | Painless hard chancres (Primary); maculopapular rash (Secondary); neurovascular gummas (Tertiary) | **CURABLE** (Penicillin G) |
| **Gonorrhea** | *Neisseria gonorrhoeae* | Gram-Negative Diplococcus | Purulent urethral discharge, severe dysuria, burning sensation, pelvic inflammation | **CURABLE** (Ceftriaxone) |
| **Chlamydiasis** | *Chlamydia trachomatis* | Obligate Intracellular Bacteria | Mucopurulent cervicitis, urethritis, asymptomatic pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) | **CURABLE** (Azithromycin / Doxycycline) |
| **Trichomoniasis** | *Trichomonas vaginalis* | Flagellated Protozoan | Foul-smelling, greenish-yellow frothy vaginal discharge, vulvar pruritus, dyspareunia | **CURABLE** (Metronidazole / Tinidazole) |
| **AIDS** | Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) | Enveloped ssRNA Retrovirus | Progressive depletion of $\text{CD4}^+$ T-helper lymphocytes, opportunistic fatal infections | **INCURABLE** (Managed by ART) |
| **Hepatitis B** | Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) | Enveloped dsDNA Hepadnavirus | Acute/chronic hepatitis, jaundice, liver cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma | **INCURABLE** (Preventable by HBV vaccine) |
| **Genital Herpes** | Herpes Simplex Virus 2 (HSV-2) | Enveloped dsDNA Herpesvirus | Painful, recurrent erythematous vesicles and ulcerating fluid-filled blisters on genitalia | **INCURABLE** (Suppressed by Acyclovir) |
| **Genital Warts** | Human Papillomavirus (HPV 6, 11) | Non-enveloped dsDNA Papillomavirus | Anogenital condyloma acuminata; oncogenic types ($16, 18$) cause **Cervical Cancer** | **INCURABLE** (Preventable by Gardasil vaccine) |

### 8.2 Long-Term Clinical Complications of Untreated STIs
1. **Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)**: Ascending infection of the uterus, Fallopian tubes, and ovaries causing extensive fibrosis and chronic pelvic pain.
2. **Tubal Infertility & Ectopic Pregnancy**: Chronic salpingitis causes scarring and stricture of Fallopian tubes, blocking ovum/embryo transit.
3. **Perinatal Transmission**: Ophthalmia neonatorum in newborns exposed to *N. gonorrhoeae* or congenital syphilis causing Hutchinson's triad.

conceptBreakdown.heading: VDRL and TPHA Diagnostic Serology
conceptBreakdown.title: VDRL and TPHA Diagnostic Serology
conceptBreakdown.content: Syphilis screening uses the non-treponemal Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) / RPR test to detect anti-cardiolipin antibodies, confirmed by the specific Treponema Pallidum Hemagglutination Assay (TPHA).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Window Period and ELISA Testing in HIV
conceptBreakdown.title: Window Period and ELISA Testing in HIV
conceptBreakdown.content: The window period is the 2-12 week interval between initial HIV infection and the appearance of detectable anti-HIV antibodies by 4th-generation ELISA (combining p24 antigen and antibody detection).
